snippet.title: The Flying Tigers - America's Forgotten Heroes | Episode 4: Endgame | FD History
snippet.description:
The Flying Tigers - Episode 4: Endgame | History Documentary

Catch up on all 'The Flying Tigers' episodes here: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfMrqOdrCidQIzVsCVJ91vwbTWO9YPjgm

In this episode:
In April 1943, two of America's most influential commanders in the China-Burma-India Theatre arrived in Washington with competing visions for the war against Japan. Major General Claire Lee Chennault, leader of the legendary Flying Tigers, argued that increased air power could cripple Japanese forces and secure victory in China. General Joseph Stilwell, meanwhile, believed that modern weapons, supplies, and training for Chinese ground troops were the key to defeating Japan.

Their disagreement sparked a high-stakes struggle over Allied strategy in Asia, placing President Franklin D. Roosevelt in the difficult position of choosing between two vastly different approaches to the war. The decision would shape the future of the campaign in China and influence the course of the Pacific War.

The series:
During World War II, a legendary group of American fighter pilots became famous for defending China against Japanese air attacks. Known as the Flying Tigers, these US airmen operated from bases in western China and played a crucial role in the early air war in the Pacific.

Formed before the United States officially entered the war, the Flying Tigers fought against overwhelming odds and quickly earned a reputation for their daring tactics and fierce resistance. Some historians believe their growing presence in the Far East increased tensions with Japan and contributed to the chain of events that ultimately led to the attack on Attack on Pearl Harbor.

From December 1941 to June 1942, the Flying Tigers provided vital aerial defence for China during one of the darkest periods of the war. Their story is one of courage, sacrifice, and innovation — yet much of it has remained untold. Until now.

snippet.title: Rockefeller’s System: The Trap You Were Born Into
snippet.description:
John D. Rockefeller didn’t just build an oil empire — he engineered the operating system of modern power. A system so deeply embedded into corporations, governments, finance, healthcare, and global markets that escaping it is nearly impossible.

1870: A young businessman in Cleveland refines 4% of America’s oil.
1880: He controls 90%.
1904: He directs the flow of 91% of U.S. oil production and 85% of final sales.

But the real story isn’t Standard Oil.
It’s what came after Standard Oil.
The corporate blueprint Rockefeller created didn’t vanish in 1911. It multiplied. It spread. It shaped the world you live in today — your job, your bills, your medicine, your bank, your technology, your food, your debt.

In this video, we break down how Rockefeller designed the foundations of the modern control structure:

• Vertical Integration — owning every step of production, from raw materials to distribution, giving him cost advantages no competitor could survive.
• Horizontal Consolidation — buy rivals or bankrupt them; eliminate competition until only one empire remains.
• The Corporate Trust — a new business structure that became the template for every major corporation today.
• Regulatory Capture — influencing the laws, the regulators, and the rules so the system always bends toward the empire.
• Philanthropy as Power — foundations that shaped medicine, education, policy, and public perception while preserving generational wealth.

The breakup of Standard Oil didn’t destroy Rockefeller — it made him richer than ever.
Exxon, Mobil, Chevron, Amoco, Sohio… the pieces of his empire simply evolved into the giants that now shape global markets.

Rockefeller didn’t just build a company.
He built the architecture of control — and its influence still surrounds you in 2025.

snippet.title: THE BIG CREATINE LIE...
snippet.description:
Most of us have been taught that creatine is strictly for sports performance.

The clinical data tells a completely different story.

It's the most researched supplement on earth. Studied for nearly 200 years, but are we still missing the point?

This is why I sat down with Dr Darren Candow. He is one of the world’s most published researchers on creatine and ageing. He’s published more than 175 scientific papers, over 115 of them focused specifically on creatine and longevity.

I was shown me the data on why muscle loss starts happening decades earlier than we think, the exact mistake millions of us make with protein as we get older and what the clinical evidence actually says about creatine for women, children, and brain health.

We discussed things like:

- 5 biggest myths about creatine.
- Why creatine is no longer just for athletes.
- What women need to know about creatine.
- Is creatine is safe for children?
- How muscle loss begins much earlier than most people realise.
- The protein mistake many people make as they age.

What blew my mind during this chat is how far the science goes beyond sport and that creatine might be one of the most misunderstood supplements in the world.

But Darren’s research points to something much bigger…

If you care about staying strong and independent as you get older, I think this conversation is worth your time.

snippet.title: Road to Defeat: Adolf Hitler's Fatal Mistakes | Free Documentary History
snippet.description:
Hitler's Lost Battles | History Documentary

Watch 'The Third Reich in Colour' here: https://youtu.be/raaqErbNeI0

At the height of World War II, Adolf Hitler appeared unstoppable. Within a few years, Nazi Germany had conquered much of Europe and stood on the brink of victory. Yet a series of fateful decisions would ultimately transform military success into catastrophic defeat.

From the halt of German forces at Dunkirk and the missed opportunity to knock Britain out of the war, to the disastrous shift in strategy during the Battle of Britain, Hitler repeatedly ignored military advice in favour of his own instincts. His invasion of the Soviet Union opened the largest front in history, while his declaration of war on the United States brought another powerful enemy into the conflict.

As the war turned against Germany, Hitler's interference became even more destructive. Refusing to allow retreats at Stalingrad, misjudging the Allied invasion of Normandy, and launching a final offensive in the Ardennes despite dwindling resources, he squandered Germany's remaining strength while Allied armies closed in from east and west.

Drawing on historical analysis and eyewitness accounts, this documentary examines the key decisions that shaped the course of the war and reveals how Hitler's strategic miscalculations contributed to the downfall of the Third Reich.

snippet.title: The British Empire’s Final Mistake — And Why America Is Repeating It
snippet.description:
October 24th, 1929. In just 6 hours, the United States lost 14 billion dollars and entered the worst economic crisis in modern history. But what few people know is that this collapse began with the decision of just one man: Charles Mitchell, America's most popular banker. In this video, we reveal how Mitchell revolutionized Wall Street by allowing millions of ordinary Americans to buy stocks with only 10% down payment, creating a debt pyramid that seemed brilliant until it imploded. Seven months before the crash, when the Federal Reserve tried to contain rampant speculation, Mitchell publicly defied the central bank by promising "unlimited liquidity" to the market. That decision accelerated the final phase ofmania that would destroy an entire generation's economy.

Mitchell's story isn't about villainy, but about how good intentions can generate catastrophic consequences. Today, with 50 million Americans trading stocks through apps, margin loans at record levels of 900 billion dollars, and promises of "financial democratization" echoing everywhere, the parallels with 1929 are terrifying. This documentary reveals the behind-the-scenes of the 20th century's greatest financial collapse and shows why the same traps are being set right now, with new technology but identical psychology. snippet.description:

Debt is a zero-sum game. For every borrower, there's a lender. If the world owes $317 trillion, someone owns $317 trillion in assets. WHO?
